# A geological map, step by step

You draw **contacts** and say **which unit** lies where; PRo3D derives the units and drapes them
on the terrain. Reference: [GeologicalMap.md](GeologicalMap.md).

> **Made-up example.** Units A–E and their outlines are invented to show the workflow on the
> Dimorphos model; they say nothing about its geology.

*Pictures generated by `tests-ui/tests/geological-map-story.spec.ts`.*

---

### 1. An empty group

![Dimorphos, nothing mapped yet](images/geological-map/story/01-dimorphos.png)

The map's contacts and labels go into one annotation group, here *Dimorphos geology*, made active
in the Annotations panel.

### 2. A new map

![The Geological Maps panel with the new map](images/geological-map/story/02-new-map.png)

*Geological Maps* panel → **New map from group**. The map is active: what you draw now belongs to it.

### 3. A closed contact

![A closed contact: two units, both unassigned](images/geological-map/story/03-first-contact.png)

A polygon divides the body into **two units**, inside and outside. Hatched: no unit assigned yet.

### 4. The legend

![Legend with two units](images/geological-map/story/04-legend.png)

**New unit** twice; give each a code and a name (`A`, `B`).

### 5. Assigning units

![Both units assigned](images/geological-map/story/05-assigned.png)

Paint brush tool: pick a unit in the legend, click into an area. One click per area.

### 6. A new contact, snapped

![Green marker: the click lands on the contact](images/geological-map/story/06-hover-snap.png)

To divide A, draw a contact across it. Near an existing contact a **green marker** shows where the
click will land - exactly on it.

### 7. The preview

![The cut across A, both ends attached](images/geological-map/story/07-preview.png)

While drawing: the new contact in yellow, the unit it cuts lit up, ends **green** when attached.

### 8. The split

![A split; the new part unassigned](images/geological-map/story/08-split.png)

Enter: A is split, the new part is hatched.

### 9. A third unit

![Unit C assigned](images/geological-map/story/09-third-unit.png)

**New unit** `C`, one click.

### 10. A unit inside a unit

![An ellipse inside A](images/geological-map/story/10-crater.png)

An **ellipse** (three clicks: long axis, then width) is a closed contact: a new unit inside A,
which becomes a ring around it.

![Unit D assigned](images/geological-map/story/11-crater-assigned.png)

`D`, one click.

### 11. Dividing the ring

![Second connecting line, both ends attached](images/geological-map/story/12-connect-preview.png)

A first line from A's outline to the ellipse only ties the two together - no new unit, no open end.
A second line closes off part of the ring...

![The ring cut in two](images/geological-map/story/13-ring-cut.png)

...a new unit, hatched,

![Unit E assigned](images/geological-map/story/14-terrace.png)

assigned `E`.

### 12. Checking

![An open contact end, marked red](images/geological-map/story/15-open-end.png)

A contact that reaches no other contact separates nothing; its ends are marked **red**...

![The problem list](images/geological-map/story/16-problems.png)

...and listed in the panel. Click an entry to fly there, **N** for the next one.

---

Units are never drawn or edited directly: each boundary is drawn once as a contact, and changing a
contact updates the units on both sides. Everything is saved with the scene; older PRo3D versions
open it with contacts and labels as ordinary annotations.
